steps.text:
Turn 306 actions are done. Here's what I found and did.

**The situation:** Korea is dominant — score 1406 vs Macedon's 855, #1 in military, GNP, and goods, and heading into a Golden Age. Science is the clear win path (64 techs, tied for the lead), and the diary was empty so I rebuilt the picture from live state.

**The bottleneck:** Both Earth Satellite and Moon Landing are already tech-unlocked, but I have **zero completed spaceports** — that single gap is the entire thing standing between me and the space race. Four cities are building them (Gyeongju fastest at 7 turns). Districts can't be gold-purchased, so I attacked the problem indirectly:

- **Bought a Fossil Fuel Power Plant in Jeonju (1440g)** — it had an Industrial Zone and Factory but no power plant while building a Spaceport, so this feeds the critical path directly.
- **Swapped the Military policy** from Resource Management (completely dead — every strategic stockpile is capped at 100/100) to Levée en Masse, cutting unit maintenance from 366 to 293/turn across my 51 units.

**Worth flagging honestly:** the policy swap charged a ~845g change fee, dropping the treasury to **-513**. At +1060/turn it returns positive (~547) next turn, so there's no disband risk, but the fee was steeper than I expected for a +73/turn gain — about a 12-turn payback.

**The key discovery for future turns:** Great Engineer **Robert Goddard** grants +20% production toward space race projects in *all* cities. I'd never earn him naturally (21/660 points), but he can be patronized for 9785g — roughly 10 turns of income, timing neatly with the spaceports finishing. I checked Democracy to halve that cost, but it needs the Suffrage civic; my current Space Race civic (5 turns) is the better pick anyway since it leads toward the space-project policy card.

I left research (Guidance Systems, 1 turn, boosted) and all city production alone — they were already correct. All 51 units had 0 moves remaining, so no unit actions were possible, and the two "CAN ATTACK" targets the city list reported were actually out of range.

**Summary:** Diagnosed the missing spaceport as the sole barrier to a science victory, bought Jeonju a power plant to speed it, cut ~73g/turn of dead maintenance, and identified Goddard (+20% space project production) as the key ~10-turn gold target.

steps.text:
Turn 307 is set up. Here's what I did and what it cost.

**The position:** Korea is running away with it — score 1407 vs 863 for second place, 65 techs vs 53 for the nearest rival, and the largest military on the map. Nobody has a Spaceport yet, and four of my cities are mid-build on one. Science victory is the obvious path, and there's no real time pressure (turn 500 is 193 turns away).

**Actions taken:**
- **Research was empty** — set Lasers, which opens the path toward Offworld Mission (needed for the final space project).
- **Two cities were building nothing** — Busan now runs a repeatable science project, Gwangju builds a Market. (A Seowon had no legal tile there, so I adjusted.)
- Switched **Merchant Republic → Communism**, filled three new policy slots, upgraded an Anti-Air Gun to a Mobile SAM, dispatched two idle builders, and sent an idle Great Musician toward a Broadcast Center with a free slot.

**The honest caveat on the government switch:** it was not the clean win I expected. Production rose 706 → 803 (+14%), shaving a turn off three Spaceports — but it cost 92 science, 43 culture, and ~300 gold/turn. I judged that acceptable because production is the binding constraint on Spaceports and space projects, and gold cannot buy districts. But it's close to a wash, not a clear gain, and it's worth revisiting once gold rebuilds. I also caught one outright mistake in my own card choice — I'd swapped Levée en Masse for the strictly weaker Conscription, raising maintenance; reverting it recovered ~40 gold/turn.

I deliberately declined the attacks the city panels offered — those units belong to Egypt, a Declared Friend. Starting a war would risk a position I'm winning peacefully.

**Next lever worth watching:** Great Engineer Robert Goddard gives +20% space-project production empire-wide for 9605 gold — roughly 12 turns away at the reduced income, which is the main cost of the Communism switch.

One-line summary: Set research to Lasers, fixed two idle cities, and switched to Communism for +14% production toward four in-progress Spaceports — at a real cost of 92 science and ~300 gold/turn, a closer trade than intended.

steps.text:
All three policy slots confirmed. Levée en Masse's real effect turned out to be −2 gold/unit maintenance (~102g/turn across 51 units) — an easy trade at +762 gold/turn to unblock the resource that gates my win condition.

**Turn 308 complete.** Here's what I found and did:

**The situation:** Korea is dominant — score 1414 vs 863 for second, 65 techs vs 53, and #1 in gold, production, and military (2501 vs 785 for the nearest rival). Science victory is wide open: nobody on the map has a Spaceport, and five of my cities are building one.

**Actions taken:**
- **Jinju was building nothing** — 104 production idling. It's fully built out (no valid Spaceport or Industrial Zone tile remains), so I put it on a Seowon science project.
- **Two policy slots were sitting empty.** Since my science is 5 techs ahead and I only need Robotics + Nuclear Fusion, *production* is the real bottleneck — space projects cost thousands. Craftsmen + Urban Planning added ~21 production/turn, concentrated in the Spaceport cities (Jeonju 149→154, Daegu 138→143, Chuncheon 109→112). Verified in-game.
- **Caught an aluminum deficit at −1/turn.** Aluminum is consumed by Spaceports and space projects, and the deficit would deepen as more Spaceports finish — a quiet way to stall the victory. Swapped the dead Levée en Masse card for Resource Management and sent a builder toward the unimproved Aluminum at (66,29).
- **Builders dispatched:** farm at (72,38), mine at (73,29) feeding Spaceport-city Jeonju.

**Two traps avoided:** Both cities flagged "CAN ATTACK" targets, but the map check showed the Field Cannon at (75,30) belongs to **Brussels** and the builder at (108,22) to **Cardiff** — city-states, not barbarians. I'm actually *suzerain of Brussels*. Attacking either would have cost me a suzerainty and standing with America for nothing.

**Held deliberately:** 1931 faith toward Great Engineer Robert Goddard (4725f), who grants +20% space-project production empire-wide — the single best purchase for this win path. Also holding 1863 favor to strip rival Diplomatic Victory Points at the Congress in 23 turns (Russia is at 8/20).

I did not end the turn, as instructed.

**Summary:** Fixed Jinju's idle production, filled two empty policy slots and swapped a dead war card for Resource Management to unblock an aluminum deficit gating my space projects (+21 production/turn into Spaceport cities), dispatched three builders, and avoided attacking two city-state units the UI flagged as targets — one of them my own suzerain.

steps.text:
Both policy slots confirmed filled. Here's what I did on turn 309.

Korea is dominant (score 1421 vs Macedon's 864, 65 techs to next-best 53, military 5× everyone) and at peace with all 11 civs, so I played it as a pure science-victory optimization turn rather than anything military. Four spaceports are already under construction, with Gyeongju's finishing in 4 turns, and Earth Satellite is unlocked and waiting on it.

The most valuable find was pure waste: **two policy slots were sitting empty.** Filling them with Levée en Masse and Urban Planning cut unit maintenance from 371 to 295 (income **+697 → +773/turn**) and added +1 production in all 9 cities. Similarly, one of nine trade route slots was unused, so I bought a Trader to fill it (~50 gold/turn that was being left on the table).

Other actions: both idle cities put to work (Gwangju → Industrial Zone; Strängnäs → bought a Monument for loyalty and set a Granary — it had *rebelled*, and I confirmed the pending "keep" decision); killed the barbarian AT Crew threatening Chuncheon with two bomber strikes; started a builder on a mine and set Busan to food focus (it was 18 turns from growing).

Two things worth flagging. Mozart **can't activate** — every Music great-work slot is full, so he and Chopin are both dead weight; that settles the faith question, and I'm banking the 2121 faith toward Great Engineer Robert Goddard (4635f), whose +20% space-race project production is the single best accelerator available. Second, the Tank couldn't reach the last barbarian Field Cannon — that whole northeast pocket is Cardiff city-state territory and we lack Open Borders, so Pyongyang/Strängnäs units are effectively fenced in. Worth getting suzerainty over Cardiff if that area matters. Also note 1884 favor is idle with the World Congress 22 turns out; a "Diplomatic Victory (+2 DVP)" resolution is queued and we're at 10/20 — that vote should target Korea, not Russia.

**Summary:** Filled two empty policy slots (+76 gold/turn, +9 production) and an unused trade route, put both idle cities to work, cleared a barbarian, and set the empire to bank faith for Great Engineer Goddard ahead of Gyeongju's spaceport completing in 4 turns.

steps.text:
Policy confirmed — Natural Philosophy is in slot 9 with every other card preserved. Here's where turn 310 stands.

**Summary:** Korea is running away with the game (score 1426 vs. 872 for second-place Macedon, #1 in military/GNP/goods, tech leader at 66 techs, and at peace with every civ) — so I pushed hard on the science victory: fixed the stalled research, filled an empty policy slot, and cleared a barbarian.

What I actually did:

- **Fixed an idle research queue.** Nothing was being researched at all, burning 555 science/turn. Set Nuclear Fusion, which together with Robotics unlocks Offworld Mission — the one tech gating the Exoplanet Expedition, the last locked link in my space chain.
- **Filled an empty Economic policy slot** with Natural Philosophy (+100% Campus adjacency), which compounds across my four Seowons. It had simply been left vacant.
- **Killed a barbarian Ranger** adjacent to my Tank at (107,17) — clean kill, 1 damage taken.
- **Dispatched two idle builders** toward unimproved Ivory and Diamonds, and **set Busan to Food focus** — it was stagnating at 17 turns to grow.

Two things worth knowing for next turn:

The Spaceport situation is better than the victory screen suggests. It reports "0 spaceports," but that's counting *completed* ones — Gyeongju (3 turns), Jeonju (5), Daegu (7), and Chuncheon (7) are all mid-build, and Earth Satellite and Moon Landing are already tech-unlocked and waiting on them.

I deliberately held the treasury rather than spending it. At 891 gold I couldn't afford the two things actually worth buying: the Royal Society government building (1760g, affordable in ~2 turns) lets Builders be consumed directly into Space Race projects, and Great Engineer Robert Goddard (4545 faith, I have 2315) grants +20% space-project production empire-wide plus a tech boost. Both are far better value than anything under 891g. Also flagging that **Gyeongju, my capital and best production city, has no Industrial Zone at all** — once its Spaceport finishes, that district plus a bought Factory is the biggest available production gain for the launch phase.

steps.text:
Done. Here's what I found and did.

**Situation:** Korea is dominant at turn 311 — score 1428 vs 872 for second place, tech lead (66 techs), military 2580 (4x the average), and at peace with everyone. The recommended path is Science, and four Spaceports are already under construction (Gyeongju 2 turns, Jeonju 4, Daegu and Chuncheon 6). Both Launch Earth Satellite and Moon Landing are tech-unlocked and just waiting on a Spaceport to finish.

**The main play** was an empty Military policy slot. **Integrated Space Cell** (+15% production toward Space Race projects in cities with a Military Academy or Seaport) was sitting unused — I slotted it, then bought a Military Academy in Daegu for 1320g so that Spaceport city qualifies too. Jeonju already had a Seaport. I also filled the empty Economic slot with Urban Planning (+1 production in all nine cities).

**Other fixes:** no civic was being researched at all, so I set Suffrage (boosted, 7 turns). Jinju was building nothing — it's at its district cap and can't site a Spaceport or Industrial Zone, so I put it on a Campus project for Great Scientist points. An idle trader was collecting nothing; I routed it to Jeonju.

Two things I deliberately did **not** do: the "CAN ATTACK" flags on Daegu and Jeonju were misleading — both Free City targets are 3 tiles away, outside the 2-tile city range, so no attack was possible. And I left gold at ~350 rather than spending further, because **Robert Goddard** (Great Engineer, +20% space-race production in *every* city) costs 8885g and income is +776/turn — he's affordable around turn 321 and is worth banking for.

Research stays on Nuclear Fusion, which gates Offworld Mission and the Exoplanet Expedition project.

One note for whoever plays next: this game has no diary entries at all, so there's no strategic memory to recover after a compaction. Since the host owns `end_turn` (where reflections are normally recorded), I couldn't add one.

**Summary:** Turn 311 Korea — slotted Integrated Space Cell +15% and bought Daegu a Military Academy to accelerate four in-progress Spaceports, fixed the missing-civic and idle-city/trader blockers, and banked gold toward Great Engineer Goddard (+20% space production) around turn 321.

steps.text:
Done. Here's what I found and did on turn 312.

**Position:** Korea is dominant — score 1432 vs Macedon's 877, rank #1 in military (2543), GNP (+789/turn), and goods, with a tech lead at 66 techs.

**The key strategic read:** `get_victory_progress` reports "0 spaceports" and recommends Science, which looks alarming — but it's misleading. Four cities (Gyeongju, Daegu, Jeonju, Chuncheon) are already mid-build on Spaceport districts, with Gyeongju finishing **next turn**. Earth Satellite and Moon Landing are both already unlocked, so the space chain starts immediately once that district lands. Exoplanet Expedition needs Offworld Mission, which isn't reachable on the tech tree yet, so I left Nuclear Fusion (50% done, 3 turns) alone rather than churn research.

**Actions taken:**
- **Cleared the one real blocker** — Pyongyang was building *nothing*. No valid district tiles there (land-constrained), so I set a Shipyard to leverage its existing Harbor.
- **Bought a builder in Pyongyang (660g)** to work the URGENT unimproved Aluminum at (114,22) — aluminum feeds spaceports and space projects, and my nearest other builder was 40 tiles away. It has no moves this turn but starts next turn.
- **Banked faith deliberately.** I have 2702 faith and Great Engineer Robert Goddard costs 4365 — he grants **+20% production on space race projects** plus a tech boost, directly on my win path. I passed on affordable-but-useless options (Chopin, 1163f) to save for him.
- Dispatched a builder toward the farm at (80,34) to fix Chuncheon's 21-turn growth stall, and upgraded my obsolete Fighter to a Jet Fighter.

**Two things worth flagging to you as tool bugs:** `get_cities` printed `>> CAN ATTACK` hints for Jeonju and Pyongyang, but both targets were 3 tiles away against a city range of 2 — both attacks failed with `OUT_OF_RANGE`. Separately, `get_units` listed Egypt under "Nearby threats," but I'm actually at **peace** with Egypt (`NOT_AT_WAR` on attack). Both hints are computed without checking range/war state, so they invite wasted or wrong moves.

Congress is 19 turns out, so my 1946 favor stays banked — no votes to queue. I did not end the turn.

One-line summary: Cleared Pyongyang's production blocker and bought a builder for its Aluminum, confirmed four Spaceports are already inbound (Gyeongju next turn) for a science win, and banked 2702 faith toward Great Engineer Goddard's +20% space-project boost.

The World Congress is 19 turns out, so there's nothing to queue — and I noticed the active Global Energy Treaty bans Nuclear Power Plants, which means Nuclear Fusion's boost is unavailable to me (it still finishes in 3 turns regardless).

Here's where turn 312 stands:

**Blocker cleared.** Slot 9 now holds Natural Philosophy. It stacks with the already-slotted Five-Year Plan to double Seowon adjacency across five campuses — the best economic card available given my situation. I ruled out the alternatives on evidence rather than vibes: Collectivization looked tempting until I checked the routes and found only 1 of 9 is domestic, and the gold/tourism cards (Free Market, Triangular Trade, Heritage Tourism) are dead weight when I'm already at +788 gold with a 336-tourist culture gap I'm never closing.

**The strategic picture is better than the victory tracker suggests.** It reports 0 spaceports, but that's a timing artifact — four cities are mid-build on Spaceport districts, with Gyeongju finishing next turn and Jeonju, Daegu, and Chuncheon following within five. Earth Satellite and Moon Landing are already tech-unlocked and waiting on exactly that. Research is correctly on Nuclear Fusion, which gates Offworld Mission and the final Exoplanet project, so I left it alone.

**Faith plan:** I deliberately did *not* spend the 2702 faith. Robert Goddard (+20% space-project production, plus a tech boost) costs 4365 faith and is precisely the Great Person this game wants; the affordable ones, Breedlove and Chopin, are tourism plays that do nothing for me. Banking a few turns for Goddard beats spending now.

**One thing I could not fix, flagged rather than papered over:** a barbarian Field Cannon sits at (75,30), directly adjacent to Jeonju's Spaceport district at (75,29) that completes in 3 turns. Jeonju's city center is 3 tiles away — outside its 2-tile range — and all 53 units had already spent their moves before this repair pass began, so nothing could engage it. **It's in pillage range of a spaceport on the critical path to the win.** Worth making the first order of business next turn: the Bomber at (74,29) or a Modern Armor can erase it easily with fresh moves.

No one is at war with me, and at 1432 score versus Macedon's 877 with a 2543 military that nobody approaches, the only real threat to this game is a barbarian gun next to a spaceport.

One-line summary: Filled the empty economic slot with Natural Philosophy to double Seowon adjacency, confirmed four Spaceports land within five turns on an unlocked science path, banked faith toward Great Engineer Goddard, and flagged a barbarian Field Cannon threatening Jeonju's Spaceport that no unit had moves left to kill.

No tech worth stealing (I'm the tech leader — Sweden runs 174 science to my 495), and the remaining ops would only manufacture grievances in a game I'm already winning peacefully. Leaving the spies on counterintelligence.

I've made the moves that matter. Here's where things stand:

**The big find:** Gyeongju — my capital, with a *completed Spaceport* — was building **nothing at all**. That's the science victory sitting idle. It's now running **Launch Earth Satellite** (8 turns), the first of the four space projects.

**What else I did:**
- **Dispatched a builder to the Aluminum at (114,22)**, flagged URGENT. This isn't routine tile-improvement — Aluminum is a hard requirement for space projects, so it's on the critical path. Arrives in 2 turns.
- **Confirmed research** is correctly on Nuclear Fusion (2 turns, boosted, on the space-race path).
- **Verified I'm at peace with all 11 civs.** The "CAN ATTACK" prompts at Jeonju and Pyongyang are barbarian/free-city stragglers, not a war.

**The plan for the gold:** I found **Great Engineer Robert Goddard**, whose ability is +20% space-race project production in *every* city — precisely my win condition. He costs 8525g and I hold 989g at +788/turn, so he's roughly 10 turns away. I deliberately left the gold unspent rather than burning it on Artillery upgrades I don't need at peace with a 2.5x military lead (2545 vs Russia's 1000).

**Worth flagging for later:** three more Spaceports are already under construction (Jeonju 2t, Daegu 4t, Chuncheon 4t), which will let the Mars components run in parallel. The World Congress fires in 18 turns and carries a *Diplomatic Victory* resolution granting Russia +2 VP — Russia sits at 8/20 to my 10/20, and I hold 1966 favor, so that vote is worth spending real favor on when it comes up. Mozart is a dead unit (0 charges, already expended) — no value to reclaim.

One caveat: this game has **no diary entries**, so I reconstructed everything from live state and have no record of prior strategic intent.

**Summary:** Started Launch Earth Satellite in the capital (whose finished Spaceport was idle — the single biggest miss on the board), sent a builder to critical-path Aluminum, and banked gold toward Great Engineer Goddard for +20% space-project output.

steps.text:
The blocker is cleared and the position is in good shape. Here's what I found and did.

**Filled the empty Economic slot with Natural Philosophy** (+100% Campus adjacency). This was the right card because science victory is unambiguously my path — I'm the only civ of twelve with a Spaceport, hold a 12-tech lead (66 vs Macedon's 54), and have three more Spaceports finishing in 2–4 turns with Launch Earth Satellite already underway in Gyeongju. Natural Philosophy stacks additively with the Five-Year Plan already in slot 3, so each of my five Seowons gains roughly +4 science on top of what it was making. Nothing else on the Economic list moves the needle: I'm already at +788 gold per turn, so the gold cards are dead weight, and tourism cards are pointless at 15% culture progress.

**Nothing else needed intervention.** I'm at peace with all eleven civs (allied with Ethiopia, friends with Egypt, Vietnam, and Russia), so the "can attack" flags at Jeonju and Pyongyang are stray barbarians next to cities with 400 HP walls — not worth diverting anything. All nine trade routes are running, and the World Congress is 18 turns out, so my 1966 favor doesn't need to be deployed yet.

**One thing worth flagging for coming turns:** I'm sitting on 2896 idle faith, and the Great Engineer Robert Goddard costs 4275 faith. His ability is +20% production toward space race projects in every city plus a free tech boost — the single best purchase available for the win condition. I couldn't afford him this turn, so the faith should keep banking rather than being spent on the cheap Great Musician or Great Merchant, both of which are affordable but useless to a science game. Worth patronizing him the moment faith crosses 4275.

Minor blemish I left alone deliberately: Daegu is food-stagnant and Jinju/Chuncheon are slow-growing. Collectivization would have fixed that, but Daegu's 149 production is currently building a Spaceport, and production matters more than growth this late.

**Summary:** Filled the blocking Economic policy slot with Natural Philosophy to boost my five Seowons' science, confirmed no threats or idle trade routes, and identified Great Engineer Goddard (4275 faith) as the next high-value purchase for the science win.
